title: Occupation, Detention, and the Legal Governance of War-Torn Territory
seo_title: Occupation and Detention in International Humanitarian Law
section: Use of Force and International Humanitarian Law

excerpt: Occupation and detention law govern some of the hardest legal problems in armed conflict: who controls war-torn territory, who may be detained, what protections civilians and combatants retain, and how military authority is constrained by humanitarian rules. This article examines Hague occupation law, Geneva Convention IV, Geneva Convention III, Common Article 3, internment, protected persons, prisoners of war, administrative detention, fair trial guarantees, ICRC access, deportation, transfer, settlement policy, property protection, humanitarian relief, non-international armed conflict detention, and accountability for unlawful detention and occupation practices. It also addresses Gaza, Ukraine, Palestine, Iraq, counterterrorism detention, and the relationship between international humanitarian law and human rights law. By connecting doctrine, source materials, case examples, and lawyer-facing workflows, the article shows how law regulates territorial control and detention without legitimizing conquest, domination, or indefinite military rule.
